rootCauseAnalysis.primaryFailureCause: All 3 Login requests returned HTTP 400 due to a backend database schema mismatch. The SQL query references column 'u1_0.last_login_ip' which does not exist in the PostgreSQL database. This prevented all authentication tokens (talent_token, mentor_token, enterprise_token) from being populated in the environment.
rootCauseAnalysis.cascadeEffect: Because no tokens were set, all 12 authenticated test cases (TC-TL002-PM-01 through PM-04, TC-MEN003-PM-01 through PM-05, TC-ENT001-PM-01 through PM-03) received HTTP 401 Unauthorized instead of their expected responses.
passedTests: TC-TL002-PM-05 (No token) — correctly returned 401 as expected
TC-MEN003-PM-06 (No token) — correctly returned 401 as expected
TC-ENT001-PM-04 (No token) — correctly returned 401 as expected
rootCauseAnalysis.recommendation: Fix the backend database schema: add the missing 'last_login_ip' column to the 'users' table, or update the JPA entity/query to remove the reference to that column. Once login is fixed, re-run the full collection.
